_why: Every collection the app writes for a shop is listed here with a decision:
does it travel between the cloud and the till, or does it stay where it was
written, and why. The restaurant's tables were in no list at all, so a shop
typed thirteen in the cloud and its till showed the two typed on the till,
and nobody was told. This file makes silence impossible: tests/sync-classification
fails when a collection appears in the code and not here, and the build fails
when the bundled sync agent's list disagrees with the 'synced' set below.
The gateway's scope map (Gateway apps/sync-gateway/src/collections.js) is the
authority on what syncs; 'synced' here mirrors it and the build checks the mirror.

local_only.business_device_grants: Five-second one-use Gateway device grants and counters belong only to the tenant API; never copy them to a till or another issuer.
local_only.business_decision_local: Desktop decision command outbox, one-use execution delivery and recovery journal belong to the originating installation, not generic sync.
local_only.business_push_devices: Private push registrations are bound to a Business session and never travel through device synchronization.
local_only.business_push_deliveries: Push retry leases and provider receipts belong only to the notification-delivery server.
local_only.business_decisions: Approval state and application receipts use the dedicated decision protocol, never generic collection sync.
local_only.business_notification_preferences: Per-account delivery preferences and scheduler leases belong to the authorizing Business server.
local_only.business_approval_notification_preferenc: Private approval-alert opt-ins, quiet hours and scan leases belong to the authorizing Business server, never generic device sync.
local_only.business_inbox: Private account notifications and read receipts must never use generic device synchronization.
local_only.business_reporting_requests: Short-lived Business read requests are consumed by the assigned reporting desktop through a dedicated protocol.
local_only.business_reporting_candidates: Short-lived reporting desktop presence is verified by Gateway and must not use generic synchronization.
local_only.business_reporting_audit: Publisher changes belong to the authorizing Business server and retain an atomic assignment audit journal.
local_only.business_stock_notification_preferences: Per-account stock-alert opt-ins, quiet hours and delivery cadence are private to the Business server and never use device sync.
local_only.business_stock_recipient_state: Private per-recipient stock classification, opt-in activation and pending deduplication identities; never generic device sync.
local_only.business_stock_snapshot_pages: Private bounded stock-observation transfer pages for notification revalidation; excluded from generic device sync.
local_only.business_stock_alert_batches: Private stock-alert ingestion batches and receipts belong to the Business notification server; never use generic device sync.
local_only.business_stock_alert_local: Desktop stock threshold state and pending episodes belong to this installation; never replicate through generic sync.
local_only.business_reporting_local: Local reporting assignments, snapshots and retry state belong to this desktop only.
local_only.business_reporting_publishers: Gateway-owned desktop reporting assignments must not be changed through generic device synchronization.
local_only.business_prepared_summaries: Prepared Business summaries enter through the assigned-publisher protocol, never last-writer-wins generic sync.
local_only.business_authorizations: Proof-bound browser consent requests belong only to the Business issuer; replication would permit cross-server replay.
local_only.business_sessions: Business token hashes and device revocation belong only to the issuing server and must never sync to another installation.
local_only.captain_sessions: Rotating device credentials and revocation belong only to the API that authorized the Captain phone.
local_only.captain_pair_codes: Single-use Captain approvals are issued or delivered explicitly to one server; they must never be replicated as shop data.
local_only.handsets: Handset token grants and revocation belong to the API that authorized the phone; copying them to an independent sale authority would permit cross-server access.
local_only.counters: per-machine sequence numbers; two machines must not share a counter
local_only.device_meta: what this machine knows about itself; meaningless elsewhere
local_only.data_change_log: the till's own change journal, which sync itself replaces
local_only.sso: sign-in tokens minted for this machine
local_only.razorpay_webhook: webhook receipts land on the cloud only; the till never receives them
local_only.bulk_price_updates: a job's progress on the machine running it
local_only.bulk_stock_updates: a job's progress on the machine running it
local_only.branch: a legacy alias seen in old code paths; the real collection is branches, which syncs
local_only.login_check: sign-in attempts and lockouts on this machine; another machine has its own
local_only.shadow_login_tokens: support sign-in tokens minted by the cloud for one use on one machine
local_only.user_sessions: browser and app sessions belong to the machine that opened them
local_only.ai_usage: The AI spend meter, counted where the call was made: the cloud meters the ordering page and the till meters its own screens. Rows are $inc counters, which last-writer-wins would clobber; the settings screen reads the side it is opened on.
local_only.ai_voice_sessions: Live-voice lines being metered by the cloud instance that opened them: a few minutes of clock per call, swept after two days. State of one server, not shop data.
local_only.printjobs: work waiting for a particular printer, claimed over HTTP by whichever till is allowed to. Syncing it would hand the same bill to two databases and print it twice, which is the one thing the atomic claim exists to prevent
local_only.print_tills: the key digests this shop has allowed to take its print jobs. A till has no use for the list, and copying it between installations would mean a machine allowed in one shop being allowed in another
local_only.mobile_sales: Mobile device grants and durable ingestion journal belong to the issuing server. Moving them independently would permit cross-server replay; completed sales use the normal sales sync.
local_only.mobile_catalogue_pages: Immutable pages supporting device-bound grants stay on their issuing server.
local_only.mobile_cloud_receipts: Explicit downstream gateway receipts recorded by the local signed sync component; evidence, not a second sale upload lane.
local_only.mobile_cloud_capabilities: The installed sync component's supported delivery protocol and authority belong to this installation.
local_only.mobile_grants: Mobile device grants and durable ingestion journal belong to the issuing server. Moving them independently would permit cross-server replay; completed sales use the normal sales sync.
local_only.mobile_pair_codes: Mobile device grants and durable ingestion journal belong to the issuing server. Moving them independently would permit cross-server replay; completed sales use the normal sales sync.
local_only.captain_payment_plans: Durable table payment journal belongs to the server receiving payment. Amounts and staff audit entries project onto sales and follow normal sales sync; retrying a payment must return to its issuing server.
local_only.kitchen_devices: Kitchen screen credentials belong to the issuing server and must not authorize devices on other installations.
local_only.kitchen_device_codes: Single-use kitchen pairing codes expire on their issuing server; copying them would enable cross-server replay.

undecided._note: Shop data that today stays where it was written. Each needs a decision and, if synced, a check that rows carry branch_id and license and that deletes leave a tombstone. Until decided, a till and the cloud can disagree on these exactly as they did on tables.
undecided.quotes: a quote made on the till does not exist in the cloud, and the reverse
undecided.coupons: a coupon created in the cloud cannot be redeemed on a till
undecided.coupon_redemptions: a redemption on the till is never known to the cloud
undecided.campaigns: campaigns run from the cloud are unknown to the till
undecided.campaign_sends: send history stays on the machine that sent
undecided.loyalty_ledger: points earned on the till are not visible online, and the reverse
undecided.loyalty_config: loyalty rules set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.cashback_issues: cashback given on the till is unknown to the cloud
undecided.cashback_settings: cashback rules set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.credit_settings: credit limits set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.messaging_settings: SMS and WhatsApp settings set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.customer_category: customer groups created in one place do not reach the other
undecided.denomination: cash denominations set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.payment_method: payment methods set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.roles: staff roles set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.reminder_sends: reminder history stays on the machine that sent
undecided.branch_preferences: per-branch preferences set in one place do not reach the other
undecided.transaction: customer credit transactions on the till are unknown to the cloud
undecided.payment: payment records on the till are unknown to the cloud
undecided.purchase_orders: a purchase order raised on the till is unknown to the cloud, and the reverse; receivings already sync
undecided.billing_outlets: Outlet configuration is currently scoped to its API database; cloud-to-desktop configuration sync is not yet implemented. Sales retain outlet snapshots.
